title: Random Remote Scene Crash
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.dev1

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev1 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7261) - AMD Ryzen 7 7745HX with Radeon Graphics (16 threads) - 31.18 GiB memory

### Issue description

All of a sudden out of nowhere, the following printed to the console output:
```
ERROR: core/debugger/remote_debugger_peer.cpp:150 - Condition "read != in_pos || err != OK" is true. Continuing.
ERROR: core/io/marshalls.cpp:190 - Condition "len < 4" is true. Returning: ERR_INVALID_DATA
ERROR: core/debugger/remote_debugger_peer.cpp:150 - Condition "read != in_pos || err != OK" is true. Continuing.
```
After that, I could no longer access any object in the Remote Scene and the currently opened remote object in inspector was completely frozen and stopped streaming its updated state to the inspector (the object was still working as expected in the game instance).

### Steps to reproduce

I frankly have no idea and wish I did... Since this error does not trigger the debugger, I couldn't see its stack trace either. 
It just happened all of a sudden, I wasn't even clicking anything, just watching the object's state as it was evolving over time. I was watching a `Node` object, in particular one of its arrays which holds references to entities that are `Node2D`.
